1	"""The speech legs: words into sound, and sound back into words.
     2	
     3	A voice simulation is a chat simulation with two more legs. The persona
     4	brain still writes the words — it never learns that they are spoken — and
     5	these are what carry them: a text-to-speech leg giving the persona a
     6	voice, and a speech-to-text leg turning what comes back into the
     7	transcript's ``agent`` turns. A third leg listens for *whether* anybody is
     8	speaking rather than for words — the voice activity detector. It is an
     9	internal simulator choice, not authored persona data.
    10	
    11	Both legs are ordinary Pipecat frame processors, in the two places a
    12	real provider's service sits — Cartesia or OpenAI speaking, and Deepgram
    13	or OpenAI Realtime listening —
    14	so the pipeline assembled around them is the same pipeline either way.
    15	The listening leg goes further and is a Pipecat STT service, the very
    16	class a real one subclasses; the speaking leg deliberately is not, and
    17	:class:`ScriptedTTS` says why.
    18	
    19	**Which pair is used comes only from the claimed models block.** The
    20	scripted pair is an explicit unit-test injection. Runtime work orders never
    21	fall back to it or combine it with one selected provider leg.
    22	
    23	**The scripted codec.** Scripted speech is real PCM — 16-bit signed
    24	little-endian mono, at whatever band the transport carries — and it is
    25	exactly invertible: each UTF-8 byte of the text becomes one fixed-length
    26	tone whose frequency names the byte. The STT reads nothing but the samples
    27	handed to it, so the loopback proves the whole audio path rather than
    28	smuggling the text past it, and a recording of the exchange can be read
    29	back the same way — which is how a test tells which speaker is on which
    30	channel.
    31	
    32	The tones stay under 3 kHz so that the narrowest band a connection can
    33	carry, 8 kHz telephony, still holds them.
    34	"""
    35	
    36	from __future__ import annotations
    37	
    38	import asyncio
    39	import logging
    40	import math
    41	import struct
    42	import sys
    43	from array import array
    44	from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, Awaitable, Callable
    45	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    46	from functools import cache
    47	
    48	from pipecat.audio.vad.vad_analyzer import VADAnalyzer, VADParams
    49	from pipecat.frames.frames import (
    50	    Frame,
    51	    InterimTranscriptionFrame,
    52	    StartFrame,
    53	    TextFrame,
    54	    TranscriptionFrame,
    55	    TTSAudioRawFrame,
    56	    TTSStartedFrame,
    57	    TTSStoppedFrame,
    58	)
    59	from pipecat.processors.frame_processor import FrameDirection, FrameProcessor
    60	from pipecat.services.settings import STTSettings
    61	from pipecat.services.stt_service import SegmentedSTTService
    62	from pipecat.utils.time import time_now_iso8601
    63	from pipecat.utils.tracing.service_decorators import traced_stt
    64	
    65	from .config import STT_PROVIDERS, TTS_PROVIDERS, VAD_PROVIDERS
    66	from .spec import SelectedModels
    67	
    68	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    69	
    70	SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES = 2
    71	"""16-bit signed little-endian, the one sample format the simulator carries."""
    72	
    73	SAMPLES_PER_BYTE = 240
    74	"""How many samples one encoded byte occupies — 30 ms at 8 kHz, 5 ms at 48 kHz."""
    75	
    76	SPEECH_LEVEL = 500
    77	"""The sample level, out of 32767, above which audio is somebody talking.
    78	
    79	A line is never digitally silent — it carries comfort noise, and a
    80	threshold is what tells that apart from speech. Set low enough to hear a
    81	quiet talker and high enough to ignore a line's own hiss.
    82	"""
    83	
    84	TONE_BASE_HZ = 200
    85	TONE_STEP_HZ = 10
    86	TONE_AMPLITUDE = 8000
    87	
    88	CARTESIA_SPEED_RANGE = (0.6, 1.5)
    89	"""What the cartesia mouth accepts as a speed multiplier, its own numbers.
    90	
    91	A speed outside this range is refused. The adapter never changes the value
    92	selected by the pinned TTS model."""
    93	
    94	LISTENING_READY_SECONDS = 15.0
    95	"""How long a listening leg may take to become able to hear.
    96	
    97	A streaming transcriber opens its connection in the background and
    98	*silently drops* audio handed to it before that connection is up. The
    99	first thing a voice exchange does is hand it the agent's greeting, so
   100	without this wait the first turn of a real call would vanish."""
   101	
   102	
   103	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   104	class PersonaVoice:
   105	    """The technical voice owned by the pinned TTS selection."""
   106	
   107	    voice_id: str
   108	    provider: str | None
   109	    speed: float | None
   110	
   111	
   112	def voice_from_models(models: SelectedModels) -> PersonaVoice:
   113	    """Read the technical voice from its one owner."""
   114	    return PersonaVoice(
   115	        voice_id=models.tts.voice_id,
   116	        provider=models.tts.provider,
   117	        speed=models.tts.speed,
   118	    )
   119	
   120	
   121	# -- The scripted codec ------------------------------------------------------
   122	
   123	
   124	@cache
   125	def _tones(sample_rate_hz: int) -> tuple[dict[int, bytes], dict[bytes, int]]:
   126	    """The tone for every byte at one band, and the way back.
   127	
   128	    A cosine rather than a sine so no tone opens on a zero sample: silence
   129	    is then exactly the samples nobody spoke into, which is what makes the
   130	    leading quiet before an answer measurable.
   131	    """
   132	    forward: dict[int, bytes] = {}
   133	    for value in range(256):
   134	        hertz = TONE_BASE_HZ + value * TONE_STEP_HZ
   135	        forward[value] = b"".join(
   136	            struct.pack(
   137	                "<h",
   138	                int(
   139	                    TONE_AMPLITUDE * math.cos(2 * math.pi * hertz * n / sample_rate_hz)
   140	                ),
   141	            )
   142	            for n in range(SAMPLES_PER_BYTE)
   143	        )
   144	    return forward, {tone: value for value, tone in forward.items()}
   145	
   146	
   147	def encode_speech(text: str, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   148	    """One utterance, spoken: PCM at the band the transport carries."""
   149	    forward, _ = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   150	    return b"".join(forward[byte] for byte in text.encode())
   151	
   152	
   153	def silence(seconds: float, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   154	    """Quiet of a given length, in the same sample format as speech."""
   155	    samples = int(round(seconds * sample_rate_hz))
   156	    return bytes(max(samples, 0) * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES)
   157	
   158	
   159	def leading_silence_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   160	    """How long nobody spoke at the start of one stretch of audio."""
   161	    quiet = 0
   162	    for offset in range(0, len(pcm) - 1, SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES):
   163	        if pcm[offset] or pcm[offset + 1]:
   164	            break
   165	        quiet += 1
   166	    return quiet / sample_rate_hz
   167	
   168	
   169	def duration_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   170	    """How long one stretch of audio lasts, from the samples themselves."""
   171	    return len(pcm) / SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES / sample_rate_hz
   172	
   173	
   174	def spoken_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   175	    """How long the speaking part of one stretch of audio lasts.
   176	
   177	    The quiet before a speaker starts is measured on its own, as
   178	    time-to-first-word, so the two measures add up to the whole rather
   179	    than counting the same silence twice.
   180	    """
   181	    return duration_seconds(pcm, sample_rate_hz) - leading_silence_seconds(
   182	        pcm, sample_rate_hz
   183	    )
   184	
   185	
   186	def peak_level(pcm: bytes) -> int:
   187	    """The loudest sample in one stretch of audio.
   188	
   189	    PCM is always little-endian and ``array`` holds samples in this
   190	    machine's byte order, so the two agree only on a little-endian
   191	    machine and a swap is what makes them agree anywhere else.
   192	    """
   193	    samples = array("h")
   194	    samples.frombytes(pcm[: len(pcm) // SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES])
   195	    if sys.byteorder != "little":
   196	        samples.byteswap()
   197	    return max((abs(sample) for sample in samples), default=0)
   198	
   199	
   200	def carries_speech(pcm: bytes) -> bool:
   201	    """Whether somebody is talking in this stretch of audio."""
   202	    return peak_level(pcm) >= SPEECH_LEVEL
   203	
   204	
   205	def decode_speech(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> str:
   206	    """What was said, read out of the samples and nothing else.
   207	
   208	    Alignment is not assumed. An utterance handed straight from the TTS
   209	    starts on a tone boundary, but the same audio inside a recording sits
   210	    after however much quiet the two speakers left between them, so the
   211	    reader slides a sample at a time until a tone lands and then runs
   212	    tone by tone until one does not.
   213	    """
   214	    _, backward = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   215	    width = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   216	    said = bytearray()
   217	    offset = 0
   218	    while offset + width <= len(pcm):
   219	        value = backward.get(pcm[offset : offset + width])
   220	        if value is None:
   221	            offset += SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   222	            continue
   223	        said.append(value)
   224	        offset += width
   225	    return said.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
   226	
   227	
   228	# -- The legs ----------------------------------------------------------------
   229	
   230	
   231	class ScriptedTTS(FrameProcessor):
   232	    """The persona's voice, deterministically.
   233	
   234	    Holds the voice the persona was authored with the way a real service
   235	    holds a provider voice id — the exchange is what proves the leg was
   236	    assembled from this simulation's own spec.
   237	
   238	    **Why this one is not built on Pipecat's TTS service, when the
   239	    listening leg is built on Pipecat's STT service.** That base class
   240	    regroups whatever it is given back into sentences, and it does the
   241	    grouping with NLTK, whose corpus is fetched from the internet the
   242	    first time it is wanted. On a machine without that corpus the
   243	    grouping raises, the turn's audio is dropped, and the recording
   244	    quietly loses a persona turn while the transcript still shows it —
   245	    found by starving a run of the corpus and reading the channels back.
   246	    There is no way to hand that base class a different grouper.
   247	
   248	    So this leg is a plain frame processor emitting exactly the frames the
   249	    base class emits, in the same place in the chain. A real provider is
   250	    still an ordinary Pipecat TTS service dropped into that same place —
   251	    what it is not is *this* leg's base class, and CI needs no corpus and
   252	    no network to speak.
   253	    """
   254	
   255	    def __init__(self, *, voice: PersonaVoice) -> None:
   256	        super().__init__()
   257	        self.voice = voice
   258	        self.sample_rate_hz = 0
   259	
   260	    async def process_frame(self, frame: Frame, direction: FrameDirection) -> None:
   261	        await super().process_frame(frame, direction)
   262	        # A transcription is a text frame travelling the other way — the
   263	        # agent's words on their way to the persona, never something to
   264	        # speak. The service base class draws the same line.
   265	        if isinstance(frame, StartFrame):
   266	            self.sample_rate_hz = frame.audio_out_sample_rate
   267	        if isinstance(frame, TextFrame) and not isinstance(
   268	            frame, TranscriptionFrame | InterimTranscriptionFrame
   269	        ):
   270	            await self._speak(frame.text)
   271	        await self.push_frame(frame, direction)
   272	
   273	    async def _speak(self, text: str) -> None:
   274	        if not text:
   275	            return
   276	        await self.push_frame(TTSStartedFrame())
   277	        await self.push_frame(
   278	            TTSAudioRawFrame(
   279	                audio=encode_speech(text, self.sample_rate_hz),
   280	                sample_rate=self.sample_rate_hz,
   281	                num_channels=1,
   282	            )
   283	        )
   284	        await self.push_frame(TTSStoppedFrame())
   285	
   286	
   287	class ScriptedSTT(SegmentedSTTService):
   288	    """What the agent said, read back out of the audio it arrived as.
   289	
   290	    Segmented rather than streaming, because that is what this leg
   291	    honestly is: it reads a whole stretch of speech at once. A full-duplex
   292	    line hands its pipeline one small slice of audio at a time and never a
   293	    turn, so a leg that transcribed each slice on its own would read every
   294	    utterance as a string of fragments. The base class here is the one a
   295	    local model subclasses: it buffers between the voice detector's start
   296	    and stop and calls :meth:`run_stt` once with the whole utterance.
   297	    """
   298	
   299	    def __init__(self) -> None:
   300	        super().__init__(
   301	            sample_rate=None,
   302	            settings=STTSettings(model=None, language=None),
   303	            ttfs_p99_latency=1.0,
   304	        )
   305	
   306	    @property
   307	    def wants_wav_segments(self) -> bool:
   308	        """Raw PCM, not a WAV file: the codec reads samples, not headers."""
   309	        return False
   310	
   311	    def can_generate_metrics(self) -> bool:
   312	        return False
   313	
   314	    @traced_stt
   315	    async def run_stt(self, audio: bytes) -> AsyncGenerator[Frame | None, None]:
   316	        yield TranscriptionFrame(
   317	            text=decode_speech(audio, self.sample_rate),
   318	            user_id="",
   319	            timestamp=time_now_iso8601(),
   320	        )
   321	
   322	
   323	class ScriptedVAD(VADAnalyzer):
   324	    """Hears the scripted codec exactly, and nothing else.
   325	
   326	    A voice activity detector answers one question — is somebody speaking
   327	    in this window of audio — and the scripted codec answers it without a
   328	    model: a tone is loud and quiet is exactly zero samples. So this leg
   329	    reads the samples and says so, which makes every speech boundary it
   330	    reports a sample position rather than a probability.
   331	
   332	    That exactness is what the record rests on. A window is one encoded
   333	    byte wide, so a scripted utterance begins and ends on a window
   334	    boundary at every band; the detector confirms speech one window in and
   335	    silence :data:`QUIET_WINDOWS` windows later, and both are corrected
   336	    back by exactly those windows — so the interval it hands over is the
   337	    interval that was really spoken, to the sample.
   338	
   339	    Silero is the leg a live simulation hears with; see :func:`build_vad`.
   340	    """
   341	
   342	    SPEAKING_WINDOWS = 1
   343	    """How many windows of speech confirm that somebody started talking."""
   344	
   345	    QUIET_WINDOWS = 4
   346	    """How many windows of silence confirm that they stopped. Long enough
   347	    to sit through a gap between words, short enough that the persona is
   348	    not left waiting on somebody who has finished."""
   349	
   350	    def __init__(self) -> None:
   351	        self._window_samples = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE
   352	        super().__init__(
   353	            sample_rate=None,
   354	            params=VADParams(
   355	                confidence=0.5,
   356	                # Loudness is already the whole of this leg's answer, so a
   357	                # second loudness gate could only disagree with it.
   358	                min_volume=0.0,
   359	                start_secs=0.0,
   360	                stop_secs=0.0,
   361	            ),
   362	        )
   363	
   364	    def set_sample_rate(self, sample_rate: int) -> None:
   365	        """Learn the input rate from Pipecat's start frame."""
   366	        self.params.start_secs = (
   367	            self.SPEAKING_WINDOWS * self._window_samples / sample_rate
   368	        )
   369	        self.params.stop_secs = self.QUIET_WINDOWS * self._window_samples / sample_rate
   370	        super().set_sample_rate(sample_rate)
   371	
   372	    def num_frames_required(self) -> int:
   373	        return self._window_samples
   374	
   375	    def voice_confidence(self, buffer: bytes) -> float:
   376	        return 1.0 if carries_speech(buffer) else 0.0
   377	
   378	
   379	# -- Choosing a pair ---------------------------------------------------------
   380	
   381	
   382	class SpeechFault(RuntimeError):
   383	    """A speech leg could not be built, or could not be made able to hear.
   384	
   385	    Deliberately not a ``PlugError``: that word names a platform refusing,
   386	    and this is the persona's own mouth or ears. Either way the simulation
   387	    is reported failed, and the reason on the record is what tells a
   388	    reader which of the two happened. Voice only, and raised out of the
   389	    voice conductor: the walk has no speech legs to hear one from.
   390	    """
   391	
   392	
   393	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   394	class SpeechProviders:
   395	    """The speech adapters resolved from one pinned persona version."""
   396	
   397	    stt: str = "scripted"
   398	    tts: str = "scripted"
   399	    vad: str = "scripted"
   400	    """Which leg hears *whether* the far end is speaking. ``scripted``
   401	    reads the test codec exactly and needs no model; ``silero`` is the
   402	    production detector, and it ships inside the pinned pipecat wheel, so
   403	    choosing it downloads nothing."""
   404	
   405	    stt_key: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
   406	    tts_key: str | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
   407	    """The direct credential for each selected leg."""
   408	
   409	    stt_model: str | None = None
   410	    tts_model: str | None = None
   411	    """The exact pinned models. Runtime code supplies no default."""
   412	
   413	    @classmethod
   414	    def from_models(cls, models: SelectedModels, *, vad: str) -> SpeechProviders:
   415	        """Resolve the direct adapters from the required models block.
   416	
   417	        OpenAI STT means its realtime socket. The segmented transcription
   418	        endpoint is not a second interpretation of the same selection.
   419	        """
   420	        stt = "openai_realtime" if models.stt.provider == "openai" else "deepgram"
   421	        return cls(
   422	            stt=stt,
   423	            tts=models.tts.provider,
   424	            vad=vad,
   425	            stt_key=models.stt.key,
   426	            tts_key=models.tts.key,
   427	            stt_model=models.stt.model,
   428	            tts_model=models.tts.model,
   429	        )
   430	
   431	    def checked(self) -> SpeechProviders:
   432	        """These legs, or the refusal an unrecognised provider earns.
   433	
   434	        **Refused rather than quietly downgraded to the stand-in.** Every
   435	        builder below accepts the scripted leg only for direct unit tests.
   436	        A misspelled runtime provider must not turn into a canned robot: a
   437	        typo on a settings page would otherwise produce a completed, green
   438	        simulation conducted by a canned robot, which is worse than a
   439	        failure because a failure tells the truth about what happened.
   440	
   441	        Runtime speech names come from the validated work order. The
   442	        additional scripted name exists only for explicit unit-test injection.
   443	
   444	        Called where the legs are *built*, not where they are resolved: a
   445	        chat simulation has no mouth and no ears, and must not fail over a
   446	        speech provider it was never going to use.
   447	        """
   448	        for owner, setting, chosen, allowed in (
   449	            ("persona", "STT selection", self.stt, STT_PROVIDERS),
   450	            ("persona", "TTS selection", self.tts, TTS_PROVIDERS),
   451	            ("deployment", "VAD adapter", self.vad, VAD_PROVIDERS),
   452	        ):
   453	            if chosen not in allowed:
   454	                raise SpeechFault(
   455	                    f"the {owner}'s {setting} is {chosen!r}, which is not a "
   456	                    "speech leg this simulator has; it speaks and listens "
   457	                    f"with {', '.join(allowed)}"
   458	                )
   459	        return self
   460	
   461	
   462	SCRIPTED_PAIR = SpeechProviders()
   463	"""The deterministic pair used only by direct unit-test assembly."""
   464	
   465	
   466	@dataclass
   467	class SpeechLegs:
   468	    """One simulation's mouth and ears, and how to finish with them."""
   469	
   470	    stt: FrameProcessor
   471	    tts: FrameProcessor
   472	
   473	    voice: PersonaVoice
   474	    """The exact voice pinned by this work order's TTS selection."""
   475	
   476	    listening: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]] | None = None
   477	    """Waits until the listening leg can hear, for a leg that connects."""
   478	
   479	    closers: tuple[Callable[[], Awaitable[None]], ...] = ()
   480	    """What a leg holds open beyond the pipeline's own teardown."""
   481	
   482	    async def ready(self) -> None:
   483	        """Block until a turn handed to these legs would really be carried."""
   484	        if self.listening is None:
   485	            return
   486	        try:
   487	            await asyncio.wait_for(self.listening(), timeout=LISTENING_READY_SECONDS)
   488	        except TimeoutError as never_ready:
   489	            raise SpeechFault(
   490	                "the listening leg did not connect within "
   491	                f"{LISTENING_READY_SECONDS:.0f}s; nothing said would have been "
   492	                "heard"
   493	            ) from never_ready
   494	
   495	    async def aclose(self) -> None:
   496	        """Release whatever the legs hold. Safe from every state, always
   497	        called — a pipeline that was never opened still built its legs."""
   498	        for close in self.closers:
   499	            try:
   500	                await close()
   501	            except Exception:
   502	                logger.exception("a speech leg did not close cleanly")
   503	
   504	
   505	def build_legs(providers: SpeechProviders, *, voice: PersonaVoice) -> SpeechLegs:
   506	    """The pair this simulation speaks and listens with.
   507

1	"""The speech legs: words into sound, and sound back into words.
     2	
     3	A voice simulation is a chat simulation with two more legs. The persona
     4	brain still writes the words — it never learns that they are spoken — and
     5	these are what carry them: a text-to-speech leg giving the persona a
     6	voice, and a speech-to-text leg turning what comes back into the
     7	transcript's ``agent`` turns. A third leg listens for *whether* anybody is
     8	speaking rather than for words — the voice activity detector. It is an
     9	internal simulator choice, not authored persona data.
    10	
    11	Both legs are ordinary Pipecat frame processors, in the two places a
    12	real provider's service sits — Cartesia or OpenAI speaking, and Deepgram
    13	or OpenAI Realtime listening —
    14	so the pipeline assembled around them is the same pipeline either way.
    15	The listening leg goes further and is a Pipecat STT service, the very
    16	class a real one subclasses; the speaking leg deliberately is not, and
    17	:class:`ScriptedTTS` says why.
    18	
    19	**Which pair is used comes only from the claimed models block.** The
    20	scripted pair is an explicit unit-test injection. Runtime work orders never
    21	fall back to it or combine it with one selected provider leg.
    22	
    23	**The scripted codec.** Scripted speech is real PCM — 16-bit signed
    24	little-endian mono, at whatever band the transport carries — and it is
    25	exactly invertible: each UTF-8 byte of the text becomes one fixed-length
    26	tone whose frequency names the byte. The STT reads nothing but the samples
    27	handed to it, so the loopback proves the whole audio path rather than
    28	smuggling the text past it, and a recording of the exchange can be read
    29	back the same way — which is how a test tells which speaker is on which
    30	channel.
    31	
    32	The tones stay under 3 kHz so that the narrowest band a connection can
    33	carry, 8 kHz telephony, still holds them.

    84	TONE_BASE_HZ = 200

   121	# -- The scripted codec ------------------------------------------------------
   122	
   123	
   124	@cache
   125	def _tones(sample_rate_hz: int) -> tuple[dict[int, bytes], dict[bytes, int]]:
   126	    """The tone for every byte at one band, and the way back.
   127	
   128	    A cosine rather than a sine so no tone opens on a zero sample: silence
   129	    is then exactly the samples nobody spoke into, which is what makes the
   130	    leading quiet before an answer measurable.
   131	    """
   132	    forward: dict[int, bytes] = {}
   133	    for value in range(256):
   134	        hertz = TONE_BASE_HZ + value * TONE_STEP_HZ
   135	        forward[value] = b"".join(
   136	            struct.pack(
   137	                "<h",
   138	                int(
   139	                    TONE_AMPLITUDE * math.cos(2 * math.pi * hertz * n / sample_rate_hz)
   140	                ),
   141	            )
   142	            for n in range(SAMPLES_PER_BYTE)
   143	        )
   144	    return forward, {tone: value for value, tone in forward.items()}
   145	
   146	
   147	def encode_speech(text: str, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   148	    """One utterance, spoken: PCM at the band the transport carries."""
   149	    forward, _ = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   150	    return b"".join(forward[byte] for byte in text.encode())
   151	
   152	
   153	def silence(seconds: float, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   154	    """Quiet of a given length, in the same sample format as speech."""
   155	    samples = int(round(seconds * sample_rate_hz))
   156	    return bytes(max(samples, 0) * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES)
   157	
   158	
   159	def leading_silence_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   160	    """How long nobody spoke at the start of one stretch of audio."""
   161	    quiet = 0
   162	    for offset in range(0, len(pcm) - 1, SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES):
   163	        if pcm[offset] or pcm[offset + 1]:
   164	            break
   165	        quiet += 1
   166	    return quiet / sample_rate_hz
   167	
   168	
   169	def duration_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   170	    """How long one stretch of audio lasts, from the samples themselves."""
   171	    return len(pcm) / SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES / sample_rate_hz
   172	
   173	
   174	def spoken_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   175	    """How long the speaking part of one stretch of audio lasts.
   176	
   177	    The quiet before a speaker starts is measured on its own, as
   178	    time-to-first-word, so the two measures add up to the whole rather
   179	    than counting the same silence twice.
   180	    """
   181	    return duration_seconds(pcm, sample_rate_hz) - leading_silence_seconds(
   182	        pcm, sample_rate_hz
   183	    )
   184	
   185	
   186	def peak_level(pcm: bytes) -> int:
   187	    """The loudest sample in one stretch of audio.
   188	
   189	    PCM is always little-endian and ``array`` holds samples in this
   190	    machine's byte order, so the two agree only on a little-endian
   191	    machine and a swap is what makes them agree anywhere else.
   192	    """
   193	    samples = array("h")
   194	    samples.frombytes(pcm[: len(pcm) // SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES])
   195	    if sys.byteorder != "little":
   196	        samples.byteswap()
   197	    return max((abs(sample) for sample in samples), default=0)
   198	
   199	
   200	def carries_speech(pcm: bytes) -> bool:
   201	    """Whether somebody is talking in this stretch of audio."""
   202	    return peak_level(pcm) >= SPEECH_LEVEL
   203	
   204	
   205	def decode_speech(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> str:
   206	    """What was said, read out of the samples and nothing else.
   207	
   208	    Alignment is not assumed. An utterance handed straight from the TTS
   209	    starts on a tone boundary, but the same audio inside a recording sits
   210	    after however much quiet the two speakers left between them, so the
   211	    reader slides a sample at a time until a tone lands and then runs
   212	    tone by tone until one does not.
   213	    """
   214	    _, backward = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   215	    width = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   216	    said = bytearray()
   217	    offset = 0
   218	    while offset + width <= len(pcm):
   219	        value = backward.get(pcm[offset : offset + width])
   220	        if value is None:
   221	            offset += SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   222	            continue
   223	        said.append(value)
   224	        offset += width
   225	    return said.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

   231	class ScriptedTTS(FrameProcessor):
   232	    """The persona's voice, deterministically.
   233	
   234	    Holds the voice the persona was authored with the way a real service
   235	    holds a provider voice id — the exchange is what proves the leg was
   236	    assembled from this simulation's own spec.
   237	
   238	    **Why this one is not built on Pipecat's TTS service, when the
   239	    listening leg is built on Pipecat's STT service.** That base class
   240	    regroups whatever it is given back into sentences, and it does the
   241	    grouping with NLTK, whose corpus is fetched from the internet the
   242	    first time it is wanted. On a machine without that corpus the
   243	    grouping raises, the turn's audio is dropped, and the recording
   244	    quietly loses a persona turn while the transcript still shows it —
   245	    found by starving a run of the corpus and reading the channels back.
   246	    There is no way to hand that base class a different grouper.
   247	
   248	    So this leg is a plain frame processor emitting exactly the frames the
   249	    base class emits, in the same place in the chain. A real provider is
   250	    still an ordinary Pipecat TTS service dropped into that same place —
   251	    what it is not is *this* leg's base class, and CI needs no corpus and
   252	    no network to speak.
   253	    """
   254	
   255	    def __init__(self, *, voice: PersonaVoice) -> None:
   256	        super().__init__()
   257	        self.voice = voice
   258	        self.sample_rate_hz = 0
   259	
   260	    async def process_frame(self, frame: Frame, direction: FrameDirection) -> None:
   261	        await super().process_frame(frame, direction)
   262	        # A transcription is a text frame travelling the other way — the
   263	        # agent's words on their way to the persona, never something to
   264	        # speak. The service base class draws the same line.
   265	        if isinstance(frame, StartFrame):
   266	            self.sample_rate_hz = frame.audio_out_sample_rate
   267	        if isinstance(frame, TextFrame) and not isinstance(
   268	            frame, TranscriptionFrame | InterimTranscriptionFrame
   269	        ):
   270	            await self._speak(frame.text)
   271	        await self.push_frame(frame, direction)
   272	
   273	    async def _speak(self, text: str) -> None:
   274	        if not text:
   275	            return
   276	        await self.push_frame(TTSStartedFrame())
   277	        await self.push_frame(
   278	            TTSAudioRawFrame(
   279	                audio=encode_speech(text, self.sample_rate_hz),
   280	                sample_rate=self.sample_rate_hz,
   281	                num_channels=1,
   282	            )
   283	        )
   284	        await self.push_frame(TTSStoppedFrame())

   287	class ScriptedSTT(SegmentedSTTService):

   292	    line hands its pipeline one small slice of audio at a time and never a
   293	    turn, so a leg that transcribed each slice on its own would read every
   294	    utterance as a string of fragments. The base class here is the one a
   295	    local model subclasses: it buffers between the voice detector's start

   323	class ScriptedVAD(VADAnalyzer):
   324	    """Hears the scripted codec exactly, and nothing else.
   325	
   326	    A voice activity detector answers one question — is somebody speaking
   327	    in this window of audio — and the scripted codec answers it without a
   328	    model: a tone is loud and quiet is exactly zero samples. So this leg
   329	    reads the samples and says so, which makes every speech boundary it
   330	    reports a sample position rather than a probability.
   331	
   332	    That exactness is what the record rests on. A window is one encoded
   333	    byte wide, so a scripted utterance begins and ends on a window
   334	    boundary at every band; the detector confirms speech one window in and
   335	    silence :data:`QUIET_WINDOWS` windows later, and both are corrected
   336	    back by exactly those windows — so the interval it hands over is the
   337	    interval that was really spoken, to the sample.
   338

   340	    """

   346	    """How many windows of silence confirm that they stopped. Long enough
   347	    to sit through a gap between words, short enough that the persona is
   348	    not left waiting on somebody who has finished."""
   349	
   350	    def __init__(self) -> None:
   351	        self._window_samples = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE
   352	        super().__init__(
   353	            sample_rate=None,
   354	            params=VADParams(
   355	                confidence=0.5,
   356	                # Loudness is already the whole of this leg's answer, so a
   357	                # second loudness gate could only disagree with it.
   358	                min_volume=0.0,
   359	                start_secs=0.0,
   360	                stop_secs=0.0,
   361	            ),
   362	        )

1	"""The speech legs: words into sound, and sound back into words.
     2	
     3	A voice simulation is a chat simulation with two more legs. The persona
     4	brain still writes the words — it never learns that they are spoken — and
     5	these are what carry them: a text-to-speech leg giving the persona a
     6	voice, and a speech-to-text leg turning what comes back into the
     7	transcript's ``agent`` turns. A third leg listens for *whether* anybody is
     8	speaking rather than for words — the voice activity detector. It is an
     9	internal simulator choice, not authored persona data.
    10	
    11	Both legs are ordinary Pipecat frame processors, in the two places a
    12	real provider's service sits — Cartesia or OpenAI speaking, and Deepgram
    13	or OpenAI Realtime listening —
    14	so the pipeline assembled around them is the same pipeline either way.
    15	The listening leg goes further and is a Pipecat STT service, the very
    16	class a real one subclasses; the speaking leg deliberately is not, and
    17	:class:`ScriptedTTS` says why.
    18	
    19	**Which pair is used comes only from the claimed models block.** The
    20	scripted pair is an explicit unit-test injection. Runtime work orders never
    21	fall back to it or combine it with one selected provider leg.
    22	
    23	**The scripted codec.** Scripted speech is real PCM — 16-bit signed
    24	little-endian mono, at whatever band the transport carries — and it is
    25	exactly invertible: each UTF-8 byte of the text becomes one fixed-length
    26	tone whose frequency names the byte. The STT reads nothing but the samples
    27	handed to it, so the loopback proves the whole audio path rather than
    28	smuggling the text past it, and a recording of the exchange can be read
    29	back the same way — which is how a test tells which speaker is on which
    30	channel.
    31	
    32	The tones stay under 3 kHz so that the narrowest band a connection can
    33	carry, 8 kHz telephony, still holds them.
    34	"""

   121	# -- The scripted codec ------------------------------------------------------
   122	
   123	
   124	@cache
   125	def _tones(sample_rate_hz: int) -> tuple[dict[int, bytes], dict[bytes, int]]:
   126	    """The tone for every byte at one band, and the way back.
   127	
   128	    A cosine rather than a sine so no tone opens on a zero sample: silence
   129	    is then exactly the samples nobody spoke into, which is what makes the
   130	    leading quiet before an answer measurable.
   131	    """
   132	    forward: dict[int, bytes] = {}
   133	    for value in range(256):
   134	        hertz = TONE_BASE_HZ + value * TONE_STEP_HZ
   135	        forward[value] = b"".join(
   136	            struct.pack(
   137	                "<h",
   138	                int(
   139	                    TONE_AMPLITUDE * math.cos(2 * math.pi * hertz * n / sample_rate_hz)
   140	                ),
   141	            )
   142	            for n in range(SAMPLES_PER_BYTE)
   143	        )
   144	    return forward, {tone: value for value, tone in forward.items()}
   145	
   146	
   147	def encode_speech(text: str, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   148	    """One utterance, spoken: PCM at the band the transport carries."""
   149	    forward, _ = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   150	    return b"".join(forward[byte] for byte in text.encode())
   151	
   152	
   153	def silence(seconds: float, sample_rate_hz: int) -> bytes:
   154	    """Quiet of a given length, in the same sample format as speech."""
   155	    samples = int(round(seconds * sample_rate_hz))
   156	    return bytes(max(samples, 0) * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES)
   157	
   158	
   159	def leading_silence_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   160	    """How long nobody spoke at the start of one stretch of audio."""
   161	    quiet = 0
   162	    for offset in range(0, len(pcm) - 1, SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES):
   163	        if pcm[offset] or pcm[offset + 1]:
   164	            break
   165	        quiet += 1
   166	    return quiet / sample_rate_hz
   167	
   168	
   169	def duration_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   170	    """How long one stretch of audio lasts, from the samples themselves."""
   171	    return len(pcm) / SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES / sample_rate_hz
   172	
   173	
   174	def spoken_seconds(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> float:
   175	    """How long the speaking part of one stretch of audio lasts.
   176	
   177	    The quiet before a speaker starts is measured on its own, as
   178	    time-to-first-word, so the two measures add up to the whole rather
   179	    than counting the same silence twice.
   180	    """
   181	    return duration_seconds(pcm, sample_rate_hz) - leading_silence_seconds(
   182	        pcm, sample_rate_hz
   183	    )
   184	
   185	
   186	def peak_level(pcm: bytes) -> int:
   187	    """The loudest sample in one stretch of audio.
   188	
   189	    PCM is always little-endian and ``array`` holds samples in this
   190	    machine's byte order, so the two agree only on a little-endian
   191	    machine and a swap is what makes them agree anywhere else.
   192	    """
   193	    samples = array("h")
   194	    samples.frombytes(pcm[: len(pcm) // SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES])
   195	    if sys.byteorder != "little":
   196	        samples.byteswap()
   197	    return max((abs(sample) for sample in samples), default=0)
   198	
   199	
   200	def carries_speech(pcm: bytes) -> bool:
   201	    """Whether somebody is talking in this stretch of audio."""
   202	    return peak_level(pcm) >= SPEECH_LEVEL
   203	
   204	
   205	def decode_speech(pcm: bytes, sample_rate_hz: int) -> str:
   206	    """What was said, read out of the samples and nothing else.
   207	
   208	    Alignment is not assumed. An utterance handed straight from the TTS
   209	    starts on a tone boundary, but the same audio inside a recording sits
   210	    after however much quiet the two speakers left between them, so the
   211	    reader slides a sample at a time until a tone lands and then runs
   212	    tone by tone until one does not.
   213	    """
   214	    _, backward = _tones(sample_rate_hz)
   215	    width = SAMPLES_PER_BYTE * SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   216	    said = bytearray()
   217	    offset = 0
   218	    while offset + width <= len(pcm):
   219	        value = backward.get(pcm[offset : offset + width])
   220	        if value is None:
   221	            offset += SAMPLE_WIDTH_BYTES
   222	            continue
   223	        said.append(value)
   224	        offset += width
   225	    return said.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

   231	class ScriptedTTS(FrameProcessor):
   232	    """The persona's voice, deterministically.
   233	
   234	    Holds the voice the persona was authored with the way a real service
   235	    holds a provider voice id — the exchange is what proves the leg was
   236	    assembled from this simulation's own spec.
   237	
   238	    **Why this one is not built on Pipecat's TTS service, when the
   239	    listening leg is built on Pipecat's STT service.** That base class
   240	    regroups whatever it is given back into sentences, and it does the
   241	    grouping with NLTK, whose corpus is fetched from the internet the
   242	    first time it is wanted. On a machine without that corpus the
   243	    grouping raises, the turn's audio is dropped, and the recording
   244	    quietly loses a persona turn while the transcript still shows it —
   245	    found by starving a run of the corpus and reading the channels back.
   246	    There is no way to hand that base class a different grouper.
   247	
   248	    So this leg is a plain frame processor emitting exactly the frames the
   249	    base class emits, in the same place in the chain. A real provider is
   250	    still an ordinary Pipecat TTS service dropped into that same place —
   251	    what it is not is *this* leg's base class, and CI needs no corpus and
   252	    no network to speak.
   253	    """

   255	    def __init__(self, *, voice: PersonaVoice) -> None:
   256	        super().__init__()
   257	        self.voice = voice
   258	        self.sample_rate_hz = 0
   259	
   260	    async def process_frame(self, frame: Frame, direction: FrameDirection) -> None:
   261	        await super().process_frame(frame, direction)
   262	        # A transcription is a text frame travelling the other way — the
   263	        # agent's words on their way to the persona, never something to
   264	        # speak. The service base class draws the same line.
   265	        if isinstance(frame, StartFrame):
   266	            self.sample_rate_hz = frame.audio_out_sample_rate
   267	        if isinstance(frame, TextFrame) and not isinstance(
   268	            frame, TranscriptionFrame | InterimTranscriptionFrame
   269	        ):
   270	            await self._speak(frame.text)
   271	        await self.push_frame(frame, direction)
   272	
   273	    async def _speak(self, text: str) -> None:
   274	        if not text:
   275	            return
   276	        await self.push_frame(TTSStartedFrame())

   278	            TTSAudioRawFrame(
   279	                audio=encode_speech(text, self.sample_rate_hz),
   280	                sample_rate=self.sample_rate_hz,
   281	                num_channels=1,
   282	            )
   283	        )

   287	class ScriptedSTT(SegmentedSTTService):

   292	    line hands its pipeline one small slice of audio at a time and never a
   293	    turn, so a leg that transcribed each slice on its own would read every
   294	    utterance as a string of fragments. The base class here is the one a
   295	    local model subclasses: it buffers between the voice detector's start
   296	    and stop and calls :meth:`run_stt` once with the whole utterance.

   323	class ScriptedVAD(VADAnalyzer):
   324	    """Hears the scripted codec exactly, and nothing else.
   325	
   326	    A voice activity detector answers one question — is somebody speaking

   330	    reports a sample position rather than a probability.

   332	    That exactness is what the record rests on. A window is one encoded
   333	    byte wide, so a scripted utterance begins and ends on a window
   334	    boundary at every band; the detector confirms speech one window in and
   335	    silence :data:`QUIET_WINDOWS` windows later, and both are corrected

    11	Both legs are ordinary Pipecat frame processors, in the two places a

   639	    neither substitutes nor clamps them.

   647	        raise SpeechFault("the cartesia speaking leg was chosen without a model")

   649	        raise SpeechFault("the cartesia speaking leg received a non-cartesia voice")

   651	        CARTESIA_SPEED_RANGE[0] <= voice.speed <= CARTESIA_SPEED_RANGE[1]
   652	    ):
   653	        raise SpeechFault(

   655	            f"range {CARTESIA_SPEED_RANGE[0]}–{CARTESIA_SPEED_RANGE[1]}"
   656	        )

   659	        model=providers.tts_model,
   660	        voice=spoken_with.voice_id,
   661	    )

   672	        # every sentence of every turn.

   706	def _openai_realtime_ears(
   707	    providers: SpeechProviders,
   708	) -> tuple[FrameProcessor, Callable[[], Awaitable[None]] | None]:
   709	    """What the agent said, transcribed while they are still saying it.
   710	
   711	    This is the only OpenAI STT adapter in this release. It holds a socket
   712	    open and transcribes as audio arrives. The segmented transcription
   713	    endpoint is not another interpretation of the same model selection.
   714	
   715	    **Turn boundaries stay egma's, not the provider's.** The service is
   716	    built in its local-VAD mode, so the detector that decides where a turn
   717	    ended is the same :class:`~egma_simulator.conductor._AgentEar` that
   718	    stamps the record's sample positions — one reading of the line, used
   719	    for both. Server-side detection would be a second opinion arriving on
   720	    a different clock, and the transcript and the timings would then
   721	    disagree about when the agent stopped talking. The ear sits directly
   722	    in front of this leg in the pipeline and pushes the frame it commits
   723	    on, so the two are wired together by the assembly order.
   724	
   725	    The stock service owns the rate its socket requires and converts the
   726	    pipeline audio itself.
   727	    """
   728	    from pipecat.services.openai.stt import OpenAIRealtimeSTTService
   729	
   730	    if not providers.stt_key:
   731	        raise SpeechFault("the openai_realtime listening leg was chosen without a key")
   732	    if not providers.stt_model:
   733	        raise SpeechFault(
   734	            "the openai_realtime listening leg was chosen without a model"
   735	        )
   736	
   737	    leg = OpenAIRealtimeSTTService(
   738	        api_key=providers.stt_key,
   739	        # False is this service's word for "the detector is in the
   740	        # pipeline, not on the server". Named rather than left to the
   741	        # default, because a release changing it would move where a turn
   742	        # ends without moving anything in this repository.
   743	        turn_detection=False,
   744	        settings=OpenAIRealtimeSTTService.Settings(model=providers.stt_model),
   745	    )
   746	
   747	    opened = asyncio.Event()
   748	
   749	    @leg.event_handler("on_connected")
   750	    async def _opened(_leg: object) -> None:
   751	        opened.set()
   752	
   753	    async def connected() -> None:
   754	        # **Two gates, because an open socket is not yet able to hear.**
   755	        # The service opens the connection and only then asks the provider
   756	        # to configure a transcription session; audio handed over in
   757	        # between is sent to a session that does not exist yet, and
   758	        # `run_stt` does not hold it back. The first thing a voice
   759	        # simulation does is hand this leg the agent's greeting, so
   760	        # without the second gate the first turn of a real call would
   761	        # simply be missing — the failure LISTENING_READY_SECONDS exists
   762	        # for, and the one the deepgram leg waits out the same way.
   763	        #
   764	        # The first gate is the service's own public event. The second reads
   765	        # a private flag, exactly as the Deepgram leg does. Pipecat 1.7.0,
   766	        # pinned in uv.lock, has no event for a configured realtime session;
   767	        # a rename must fail loudly here rather than make first turns vanish.
   768	        await opened.wait()
   769	        if not hasattr(leg, "_session_ready"):
   770	            raise SpeechFault(
   771	                "this pipecat release no longer says when the openai "
   772	                "realtime leg's transcription session is ready; a turn "
   773	                "spoken before it is would be lost"
   774	            )
   775	        # Polled rather than awaited, and the linter is right that an event
   776	        # would be better: the service registers `on_connected`,
   777	        # `on_disconnected` and `on_connection_error`, and none of them
   778	        # fires when the transcription session becomes configured. A flag
   779	        # is all this release offers, so a flag is what this reads. The
   780	        # caller bounds the whole wait — see LISTENING_READY_SECONDS — so a
   781	        # session that never becomes ready is a refusal rather than a hang.
   782	        while not leg._session_ready:  # noqa: ASYNC110
   783	            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
   784	
   785	    return leg, connected

1	"""The persona brain: traits and scenario in, a turn-taking speaker out.
     2	
     3	The brain owns the composition — how authored traits and the scenario
     4	become a system prompt — and the mapping between the transcript's two
     5	speakers and the model's chat roles. What actually produces words sits
     6	behind the model-client seam, so everything here is tested with the
     7	scripted client or a recording fake.

    25	    "patience": "Waits once before asking again.",
    26	    "accent": "Neutral American English.",

    34	def test_the_system_prompt_carries_all_human_traits_and_scenario():
    35	    prompt = compose_system_prompt(TRAITS, SCENARIO)

    37	    for value in TRAITS.values():
    38	        assert value in prompt
    39	    assert SCENARIO in prompt
    40	    assert CONCLUDE_MARKER in prompt
    41	    assert "stay in character" in prompt.lower()
    42	
    43

    45	    prompt = compose_system_prompt(TRAITS, SCENARIO)
    46	
    47	    assert '"voice"' not in prompt
    48	    assert '"models"' not in prompt
    49	
    50

    52	    assert compose_system_prompt(TRAITS, SCENARIO) == compose_system_prompt(
    53	        TRAITS, SCENARIO
    54	    )
    55	
    56	
    57	def test_history_maps_to_chat_roles_from_the_personas_side():
    58	    messages = messages_for(
    59	        "the prompt",
    60	        [
    61	            Turn("agent", "Hello, how can I help?"),
    62	            Turn("human", "I need to move my cleaning."),
    63	            Turn("agent", "Which day suits?"),
    64	        ],
    65	    )
    66	    assert messages == [

    68	        {"role": "user", "content": "Hello, how can I help?"},
    69	        {"role": "assistant", "content": "I need to move my cleaning."},
    70	        {"role": "user", "content": "Which day suits?"},
    71	    ]

    73

    75	    """Someone has to go first. When no agent greeting arrived, the persona
    76	    opens — and chat-shaped models want a user message to answer, so a
    77	    fixed stage-setting line stands in for the silence."""
    78	    messages = messages_for("the prompt", [])
    79	    assert messages == [
    80	        {"role": "system", "content": "the prompt"},
    81	        {"role": "user", "content": OPENING_NUDGE},
    82	    ]

    84	
    85	async def test_the_persona_speaks_through_its_model():
    86	    class RecordingModel:
    87	        def __init__(self) -> None:
    88	            self.saw: list[list[dict]] = []
    89	
    90	        async def reply(self, messages: list[dict]) -> PersonaReply:
    91	            self.saw.append(messages)
    92	            return PersonaReply(text="Hello there.", concluded=False)
    93

    99

   105	    assert SCENARIO in messages[0]["content"]
   106	    assert messages[1] == {"role": "user", "content": "Front desk, hello."}

   110	    persona = Persona(

   118	    assert first == PersonaReply(text="First thing.", concluded=False)

   123

   126	    assert third.concluded is True

    78	    schema = selection_schema(kind)

   710

   712	    open and transcribes as audio arrives. The segmented transcription
   713	    endpoint is not another interpretation of the same model selection.
   714	
   715	    **Turn boundaries stay egma's, not the provider's.** The service is
   716	    built in its local-VAD mode, so the detector that decides where a turn
   717	    ended is the same :class:`~egma_simulator.conductor._AgentEar` that
   718	    stamps the record's sample positions — one reading of the line, used
   719	    for both. Server-side detection would be a second opinion arriving on
   720	    a different clock, and the transcript and the timings would then
   721	    disagree about when the agent stopped talking. The ear sits directly
   722	    in front of this leg in the pipeline and pushes the frame it commits
   723	    on, so the two are wired together by the assembly order.

   726	    pipeline audio itself.

    38	def property_constants(node: object, property_name: str) -> set[str]:
    39	    if isinstance(node, list):

    41	        for child in node:

    44	    if not isinstance(node, dict):

    53	            if isinstance(constant, str):

550	    # default grace is ten seconds, which would kill mid-sentence.
   551	    stop_grace_period: 10m
   552	    environment:
   553	      # Where it claims, heartbeats and reports. The API and the simulator
   554	      # meet inside this network, so this is the service name rather than
   555	      # the origin a browser uses. The endpoints it dials arrive with the
   556	      # trigger; until then it asks, is told there is nothing, and asks
   557	      # again, which is what a queue with nothing in it looks like.
   558	      EGMA_SIMULATOR_CONTROL_PLANE_URL: ${EGMA_SIMULATOR_CONTROL_PLANE_URL:-http://api:3100}
   559	      # What it shows the control plane to be allowed to claim, as a bearer
   560	      # — the same header an Egma key uses everywhere else. The API checks it
   561	      # on every claim, so this reads the same variable as the api service
   562	      # above and the two halves always match. It has no default there and
   563	      # none here: one line in .env sets both.
   564	      EGMA_SIMULATOR_SERVICE_TOKEN: ${EGMA_SIMULATOR_SERVICE_TOKEN:?no default — egma_st_ then openssl rand -hex 32, set it in .env for both containers}
   565	      # How many simulations one simulator conducts at once. It claims only
   566	      # what it has room for, so a big run degrades to a queue rather than
   567	      # to overload — raise this, or start a second simulator, and they
   568	      # distribute between themselves with nothing in front of them.
   569	      # Blank means the simulator's own default of two. Compose passes the
   570	      # variable through but does not restate that default, so a bare process
   571	      # and a container cannot silently acquire different limits again.
   572	      #
   573	      # **It is also this deployment's ceiling on concurrent phone calls**,
   574	      # because a voice simulation holds a channel on the carrier trunk for
   575	      # as long as it lasts, and nothing else counts them. Two simulators at
   576	      # this number is twice this number of calls, and the trunk's own limit
   577	      # is the one that matters: past it the carrier refuses, and a refused
   578	      # call is a failed simulation rather than a queued one.
   579	      EGMA_SIMULATOR_CAPACITY: ${EGMA_SIMULATOR_CAPACITY:-}
   580	      # No model, voice or provider key is container configuration. The pinned
   581	      # persona version supplies one complete selection, and the claim adds only
   582	      # the current keys for its selected providers. Missing data is refused;
   583	      # there is no environment fallback. Internal simulator adapters remain
   584	      # fixed deployment choices, not persona or platform authoring.
   585	      # The scripted detector understands only the deterministic test codec;
   586	      # every shipped live container must use the real speech detector.
   587	      EGMA_SIMULATOR_VAD_PROVIDER: silero
   588	      # The shipped phone bridge. A work order may supply a carrier route, but
   589	      # it cannot choose or create the deployment's media backend.
   590	      EGMA_SIMULATOR_MEDIA_BACKEND: livekit
   591	      # The media server this container talks to. It is a third-party
   592	      # binary that reads its own key and secret when it is *created*, so
   593	      # it can never reach the platform's database and its address and
   594	      # credential stay bootstrap configuration on both sides. The default
   595	      # is the LiveKit beside it, filled in from the same pair the two
   596	      # containers below authenticate each other with, so the three halves
   597	      # can never disagree. That pair has no default here: `egma self-host`
   598	      # generates one for the workspace and hands it to all three, so a
   599	      # deployment never runs on a credential published in this repository.
   600	      #
   601	      # Nothing here makes this simulator dial. The connection type selects the
   602	      # plug; the platform supplies the carrier route; this deployment supplies
   603	      # the LiveKit bridge. A platform with no carrier can still run chat work.
   604	      EGMA_SIMULATOR_LIVEKIT_URL: ${EGMA_SIMULATOR_LIVEKIT_URL:-ws://livekit:7880}
   605	      EGMA_SIMULATOR_LIVEKIT_API_KEY: ${EGMA_SIMULATOR_LIVEKIT_API_KEY:-${EGMA_LIVEKIT_API_KEY:?no default anywhere — egma self-host up generates this pair and writes it to .egma-platform/platform.env}}
   606	      EGMA_SIMULATOR_LIVEKIT_API_SECRET: ${EGMA_SIMULATOR_LIVEKIT_API_SECRET:-${EGMA_LIVEKIT_API_SECRET:?no default anywhere — egma self-host up generates this pair and writes it to .egma-platform/platform.env}}
   607	      # Where recordings go. Naming an endpoint is the whole of what sends
   608	      # them to object storage; naming none keeps them in a directory on
   609	      # whatever disk the process is running on, which is what a bare
   610	      # `egma-simulator` and the test suite do. This deployment names one,

   567	EGMA_SIMULATOR_LOG_LEVEL=INFO
   568	
   569	# Which port the workbench publishes, for the dev-only overlay that starts one.
   570	# `docker compose up` starts no workbench, so this is unused until you ask for
   571	# it; see the README. It is published to 127.0.0.1 and not to the network,

   605

   608	# but give each developer and production its own SIP username/password in that
   609	# list. A credential-authenticated route supplies all four phone values. A
   610	# source-IP-authenticated carrier supplies only the trunk address and source

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/simulator_flow
Payload:
The default persona LLM receives one fixed Egma system frame, the complete persona traits, the current test’s scenario, and the full conversation history. There is no universal final prompt because the scenario changes for every test.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Test + persona identity] --> B[Run pins exact test and persona versions]
  B --> C[Claim API builds SimulationSpec v3]
  C --> D[Persona: traits + scenario + selected LLM]
  D --> E[Fixed system frame]
  E --> F{Did customer agent speak first?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Add agent words as user]
  F -- No --> H[Add hidden opening nudge as user]
  G --> I[OpenAI chat completion]
  H --> I
  I --> J[Persona reply]
  J --> K{Contains CONCLUDED?}
  K -- No --> L[Speak/send turn, add full history, repeat]
  K -- Yes --> M[Strip marker and end]
  L --> I
  M --> N[Turns/timings become OTLP spans]
  N --> O[Spans land before lifecycle report]
  O --> P[Completed simulation creates grading work]
  P --> Q[Grader reads trace + expected behaviors]
```

The exact default system prompt is:

```text
You are playing a person in a live conversation with a customer service agent. You are the person; the agent is who you are talking to.

Who you are, exactly as authored:

{
  "accent": "Neutral American English.",
  "backgroundNoise": "None.",
  "language": "en-US",
  "manner": "Clear, natural, and conversational.",
  "patience": "Starts patient and gives the agent time to explain.",
  "personality": "Speaks clear, natural English. Starts patient and cooperative, answers one question at a time, and becomes firmer if the agent is confusing or repetitive without becoming rude.",
  "underFriction": "Becomes firmer if the agent is confusing or repetitive, without becoming rude."
}

Why you are here today:

<THE TEST SCENARIO IS INSERTED HERE>

How to conduct yourself:
- Stay in character as this person for the whole exchange. Never mention being simulated, tested, or an AI.
- Speak one conversational turn at a time, in plain spoken words — no lists, no headings, no stage directions.
- Pursue what you came for until it is concluded to your satisfaction, and let your persona decide how patiently.
- When your goal is concluded and nothing further is needed, say a brief goodbye and end your reply with [CONCLUDED].
```

Exact message rules:

- `system`: prompt above.
- `assistant`: every persona/human turn.
- `user`: every customer-agent turn.
- If the customer agent has not spoken, Egma adds this hidden user message:  
  `(The conversation is open and the agent is listening. Speak your first turn.)`
- The hidden nudge is not a transcript turn.
- Every later request contains the complete accumulated history.
- The OpenAI body is only `{ model, messages }`. Egma sends no temperature, token limit, seed, tools, or sampling controls.
- `[CONCLUDED]` is removed before transcript or TTS.

The persona prompt does not receive expected behaviors, grader prompts, customer-agent configuration, organization/project names, connection credentials, mock tools, STT/TTS settings, voice ID, or recordings.

Key source evidence:

- Default traits: `packages/db/src/persona-library/catalog.ts:54-76`
- Run pins exact versions: `packages/db/src/access/runs.ts:685-747`
- Claim builds traits/models/scenario: `apps/api/src/routes/claims.ts:311-470`
- Simulator parses them unchanged: `apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/spec.py:169-244`
- Exact prompt and role mapping: `apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/persona.py:24-84`
- Exact OpenAI request and marker handling: `apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/model.py:179-247`
- Voice Pipecat path: `apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/conductor.py:436-627,815-877`
- Voice opening timing: `apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/conductor.py:977-1072`
- Spans before terminal report: `apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/service.py:375-466`
- Grading handoff: `packages/db/src/access/runs.ts:1793-1834`

One modality difference: voice speaks the final stripped goodbye before ending. Chat records that final turn but exits before sending it to the customer agent (`walk.py:215-226`).

Graphify 0.9.32 is installed, but this worktree had no existing `graphify-out`. I left extraction to the root task because this subtask was explicitly read-only. No files changed.

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/persona_models
Payload:
At local `origin/main` commit `e68cb90ce2f03bef95561718917d183e39e0aaa9`, the shared default persona uses:

| Leg | Exact selection | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| LLM | OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` | Pinned per persona version |
| STT | OpenAI `gpt-live-transcribe` | Pinned per persona version |
| TTS | Cartesia `sonic-3.5` | Pinned per persona version |
| Voice | `5ee9feff-1265-424a-9d7f-8e4d431a12c7` | Pinned with TTS selection |
| Speed | `1` multiplier | Pinned with TTS selection |

The repository has no human-readable name for that Cartesia voice ID.

Key evidence:

- The provider catalog defines these values and makes the first entry for each job the recommended selection: [catalog.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/models/catalog.ts:24), especially lines 24–60 and 71–78.
- `RECOMMENDED_PERSONA_MODELS` copies those exact selections: [selections.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/models/selections.ts:160), lines 160–189.
- Default Persona v1 pins that whole value: [catalog.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/persona-library/catalog.ts:54), lines 54–75.
- Every new project points to the same shared persona ID: [provisioning.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/access/provisioning.ts:52), lines 52–65.
- The database test proves two customers receive the same identity and exact traits/models: [provisioning-starter-persona.test.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/test/provisioning-starter-persona.test.ts:129), lines 129–159.

Ownership and fallback rules:

- LLM, STT, TTS, voice, and speed belong to an immutable persona version. Runs pin that version: [personas.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/schema/personas.ts:20), lines 20–30 and 101–118.
- Provider credentials do not belong to the persona. They are deployment-wide current credentials.
- The simulator environment cannot override the persona’s model, voice, or speed. The work order is the only source: [config.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/config.py:1), lines 1–11; [docker-compose.yml](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/docker-compose.yml:580), lines 580–587.
- Missing or invalid model data is refused. It never falls back: [model-selections.test.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/test/model-selections.test.ts:68), lines 68–81.
- `ScriptedModel` and scripted speech are test implementations only. Runtime work never falls back to them: [speech.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/speech.py:19), lines 19–21 and 431–463.
- A custom persona that omits models receives the recommended value once at authoring time. This is not a runtime fallback: [personas.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/access/personas.ts:689), lines 689–701.
- The only deployment-wide speech choice is VAD. Normal Docker Compose pins Silero. A bare Python process defaults to scripted VAD: [docker-compose.yml](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/docker-compose.yml:580), lines 580–587; [config.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/config.py:555), lines 555–613.

Credential resolution:

- If both `EGMA_PROVIDER_CREDENTIALS_SECRET_ID` and `EGMA_PROVIDER_CREDENTIALS_REGION` exist, the API uses AWS Secrets Manager. If neither exists, it reads `EGMA_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `EGMA_DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`, and `EGMA_CARTESIA_API_KEY`. A half-configured AWS source fails at startup: [index.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/provider-credentials/src/index.ts:33), lines 33–58 and 102–121.
- AWS fields are `openai_api_key`, `deepgram_api_key`, and `cartesia_api_key`. The source keeps no cross-work cache: [index.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/provider-credentials/src/index.ts:137), lines 137–185.
- The API loads the current bundle once for each simulation. Voice gets keys for all three legs; chat gets only the LLM key: [claims.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/api/src/routes/claims.ts:158), lines 158–198 and 412–430.
- For this default voice persona, the same OpenAI account key funds both LLM and STT. Cartesia gets its own key. The assembled voice-spec test proves the exact wire value: [claims-routes.test.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/api/test/claims-routes.test.ts:1029), lines 1029–1072.
- There is no credential fallback to another provider: [sources.test.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/provider-credentials/test/sources.test.ts:13), lines 13–34.
- An unreadable AWS bundle releases the simulation back to the queue. A readable bundle missing the selected provider key makes dispatch fail: [claims-routes.test.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/api/test/claims-routes.test.ts:1196), lines 1196–1241.

Adapter behavior:

- The LLM adapter accepts only `openai/gpt-4o-mini`; any other pair or missing key fails: [model.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/model.py:224), lines 224–247.
- It sends `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` with only `{model, messages}` and a bearer key. Egma sends no temperature, token limit, tools, or sampling controls. The timeout is 60 seconds: [model.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/model.py:41), lines 41–48 and 179–216.
- `[CONCLUDED]` marks the final turn and is removed from the transcript. Empty, malformed, unreachable, timed-out, or non-200 answers become model failures.
- OpenAI STT always maps to Pipecat’s realtime STT service. It receives `gpt-live-transcribe`, uses local turn detection, and waits until the realtime session can hear: [speech.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/speech.py:413), lines 413–429 and 706–785.
- Cartesia receives the pinned `sonic-3.5` model, exact voice ID, and exact speed. Egma does not substitute or clamp them. Output is raw `pcm_s16le`: [speech.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/speech.py:630), lines 630–675.
- Supported alternatives are Deepgram `nova-3-general` for STT and OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini-tts` with recommended voice `alloy` for TTS. They are explicit persona choices, not fallbacks. LLM currently has no alternative.

Focused verification command:

```sh
cd /Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_model.py tests/test_selected_models.py tests/test_streaming_legs.py -q
```

Result: `30 passed` in `7.62s`, with one upstream Pipecat deprecation warning. These tests prove the LLM request shape, exact contract-to-adapter mapping, direct-key use, realtime STT model, and unchanged Cartesia model/voice/speed.

`graphify-out` was absent when this audit began, so I told the parent task that Graphify needed a fresh extraction before its required query/rendered interpretation.

The core answer: the Default Persona is one shared, read-only Egma persona. It is not copied for each customer. Its system prompt combines: 1. A fixed Egma instruction. 2. The Default Persona’s traits. 3. The current test’s scenario. 4. The full conversation history. This is exact for current `origin/main`, commit `e68cb90ce2f03bef95561718917d183e39e0aaa9`. I did not inspect the hosted deployment, so this does not prove which commit its containers run. ## The complete flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["One shared Default Persona v1"] --> B["New project points to it"] B --> C{"Does the test name personas?"} C -- "No" --> D["Test version saves the project's default persona ID"] C -- "Yes" --> E["Test version saves the selected persona IDs"] D --> F["Run pins the current persona version"] E --> F F --> G["Claim API builds SimulationSpec v3:
traits + models + test scenario + current provider keys"] G --> H["Simulator builds the system prompt"] H --> I{"Has the customer agent spoken?"} I -- "Yes" --> J["Add agent words as role: user"] I -- "No" --> K["Add hidden opening nudge as role: user"] J --> L["OpenAI gpt-4o-mini
system prompt + full history"] K --> L L --> M["Persona reply"] M --> N{"Contains [CONCLUDED]?"} N -- "No" --> O{"Chat or voice?"} O -- "Chat" --> P["Send text to the customer agent"] O -- "Voice" --> Q["Cartesia turns text into audio"] P --> R["Customer agent answers"] Q --> S["OpenAI STT turns agent audio into text"] R --> T["Append both turns to history"] S --> T T --> L N -- "Yes" --> U["Remove marker and end"] U --> V["Store turns and timing spans"] V --> W["Finish simulation and create grading work"] ``` I refreshed Graphify for this checkout: 1,069 code files, 11,284 nodes, and 28,876 post-cluster edges. Its queries centered on `projectDefaultPersona`, `resolvePersonaVersions`, `assembledSpec`, `RunningSimulation`, `Persona`, and `messages_for`. The API-to-simulator step crosses a JSON contract, so I checked both ends directly in the source. [Open the fresh Graphify call-flow export](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/visualizations/2026/08/25/01a03642-a2bb-74d3-9510-3c7ae83c3f8c/egma-persona/egma-persona-callflow.html) ## The exact system prompt Only the marked test scenario changes: ```text You are playing a person in a live conversation with a customer service agent. You are the person; the agent is who you are talking to. Who you are, exactly as authored: { "accent": "Neutral American English.", "backgroundNoise": "None.", "language": "en-US", "manner": "Clear, natural, and conversational.", "patience": "Starts patient and gives the agent time to explain.", "personality": "Speaks clear, natural English. Starts patient and cooperative, answers one question at a time, and becomes firmer if the agent is confusing or repetitive without becoming rude.", "underFriction": "Becomes firmer if the agent is confusing or repetitive, without becoming rude." } Why you are here today: How to conduct yourself: - Stay in character as this person for the whole exchange. Never mention being simulated, tested, or an AI. - Speak one conversational turn at a time, in plain spoken words — no lists, no headings, no stage directions. - Pursue what you came for until it is concluded to your satisfaction, and let your persona decide how patiently. - When your goal is concluded and nothing further is needed, say a brief goodbye and end your reply with [CONCLUDED]. ``` The exact template and role mapping are in [persona.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/persona.py:24). The exact Default Persona traits are in [catalog.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/persona-library/catalog.ts:54). There is no single universal final prompt because every test supplies a different scenario. ## What is sent to the LLM If the customer agent has not spoken, the first request has this shape: ```json { "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": "" }, { "role": "user", "content": "(The conversation is open and the agent is listening. Speak your first turn.)" } ] } ``` If the customer agent greets first, its greeting replaces that hidden nudge. On later calls: - Customer-agent turns use `role: "user"`. - Persona turns use `role: "assistant"`. - Egma sends the complete accumulated history each time. - The hidden opening nudge is not stored as a transcript turn. Egma sends `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`. The body contains only `model` and `messages`. Egma does not set temperature, token limits, tools, seed, `top_p`, or penalties. The timeout is 60 seconds. See [model.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/model.py:179). ## Exact models for Default Persona v1 | Function | Exact selection | |---|---| | Persona LLM | OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` | | Voice transcription | OpenAI `gpt-live-transcribe` | | Text-to-speech | Cartesia `sonic-3.5` | | Cartesia voice ID | `5ee9feff-1265-424a-9d7f-8e4d431a12c7` | | Speaking speed | `1` | | Voice activity detection | Silero in shipped Docker Compose; this is deployment configuration, not persona content | The repository has no human-readable name for that Cartesia voice ID. Chat simulations use only the LLM. Voice simulations use the same LLM plus OpenAI realtime transcription and Cartesia speech. The selections come from the immutable persona version; there is no simulator model or voice fallback. See [model catalog](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/models/catalog.ts:24) and [speech.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/speech.py:413). Provider keys are separate from the persona. For each simulation, the API loads the current OpenAI and Cartesia keys from AWS Secrets Manager in Egma Cloud, or from environment variables in self-hosted Egma. Missing keys cause a failure; Egma does not silently select another provider. ## What “default for every customer” really means - Every new project initially points to this one shared persona ID: `prs_01M0E4EVJ6ECGVJEA4NSBTC0CC`. - The migration gave it only to existing projects that had no default. It preserved existing custom choices. - A project admin can choose another default persona. - A test can explicitly name another persona. - A test that names no persona saves the project’s current default persona identity. - Starting a run pins the exact persona version used by that run. Therefore, the Default Persona is available to every project and is the initial default. It is not forced into every test forever. See [project provisioning](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/access/provisioning.ts:52), [test resolution](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/access/tests.ts:672), and [run pinning](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/access/runs.ts:704). The persona LLM does not receive expected behaviors, grader instructions, project or organization names, customer-agent configuration, connection credentials, mock tools, model settings, voice ID, or recordings. Grading happens afterward as a separate process. One current difference is worth knowing: voice speaks the final goodbye after removing `[CONCLUDED]`. Chat records that final goodbye but ends before sending it to the customer agent. Focused verification passed: 26 simulator tests and 11 TypeScript model-contract tests, 37 tests total.
